records.name: Girls Inc. of Greater Philadelphia and Southern New Jersey
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps girls build confidence and leadership skills through programs such as career exploration, science and math, self-defense, money skills and summer camps. Families can enroll a girl through the site.
records.what_you_do: Families can use the Enroll a girl link on the Programs page to sign up for a program. Adults can host a career exploration, become an advocate, or join the team.

schedule.text: Out of school time programs and summer camps for girls. The site does not list meeting days, times or dates for them.

cost.text: The site does not list program fees.

first_step.how: Use the Enroll a girl link on the Programs page, which opens an online enrollment form.
first_step.basis: Anyone can start an enrollment form for a girl, but the site does not say what a first session is like or how ages are set.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists programs by topic, such as career exploration, self-defense, money skills, science and math, and early literacy for grades K to 3. It does not say how long a session runs, what it costs or how many girls attend, so ask the office before you enroll.
first_visit_tips: Ask the office about cost, age range and schedule before the first session.
The office is in the Bok building at 1901 S. 9th St., Suite 602.

records.notes: The Serve It Forward Pickleball Classic (Sunday, Nov 15, 2026, 1 to 5 pm, Ballers Social Sports) is a one-time fundraiser, so it is kept out of the schedule and used only for last_sign_of_life. The Out of School Time, Summer Camps and School and Community Based pages were located but not read because the six fetch cap was reached. The IRS contact name 'The Organization' is a placeholder and was dropped. The enrollment form was not opened or submitted. The contact page has only a form, with no phone or email published.

records.name: Give Me My Roses
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that promotes gratitude and appreciation. It runs a Women's Circle every two weeks, an arts and crafts workshop for ages 9 and up, and a recognition program at participating venues.
records.what_you_do: Join the Women's Circle by RSVP email, or ask about the arts and crafts workshop through the contact form. You can also volunteer, with roles such as community workshops, event coordination, youth mentorship and social media work.

schedule.text: The Women's Circle meets every two weeks. Dates and times are not published on the site, so RSVP by email to ask.

cost.text: The site does not list a fee for the circle or the workshop. It has a general donation link.

first_step.how: Email info@GiveMeMyRoses.org to RSVP for the Women's Circle, or use the contact form and pick Arts & Crafts Motivation to ask about the workshop.
first_step.basis: The circle takes RSVPs by email from the public. The site does not say whether it has openings or who the circle is for beyond its name.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Women's Circle is a regular meetup for planning, support and personal growth. The site does not say how long a session lasts, where it meets or what happens on a first visit, so ask when you RSVP. The arts and crafts workshop, for ages 9 and up, has people make a rose collage on canvas with their own methods, plus verbal rose exchanges and Q&A sessions about healing and equal rights.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come, since the site does not list a meeting place.
Ask about the workshop schedule and cost when you reach out, because neither is published.

records.notes: The events page lists two past events in 2026 (March 22 and April 30) and no upcoming ones, so last_sign_of_life is 2026-04. The about page names Cynthaya Johnson Summers as founder; the contact name Lonnie summers is kept from tier 1 and should be checked. The page does not say who the Women's Circle is for. The group name suggests women, but no audience tag was set. The Women's Circle has no page of its own; RSVP is by email only.

records.name: Glenwood Green Acres
records.summary: A large food-growing garden on Glenwood Avenue with 102 individual plots on about 3.67 acres, founded in 1983 and preserved in 1997. Neighbors can email the garden to ask about joining.
records.what_you_do: Grow food in an individual plot, or help with shared upkeep such as weeding, watering, planting and grounds work.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings on the second Tuesday of each month from April through October. The page gives no meeting time or place. Neighborhood work days are held, but no dates are listed.

cost.text: The page does not state plot fees or dues.

first_step.how: Email 1801glenwoodgreenacres@gmail.com to ask about a plot, or to offer help with grounds work.
first_step.basis: Anyone can email to ask about a plot or to help with upkeep. The page says plots depend on availability and gives no waitlist or open-day details.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers help with weeding, watering, planting and general grounds upkeep. Visitors can come to the monthly meetings on the second Tuesday in season, but the page gives no meeting time or place and no work-day dates, so the email is the place to ask. The page does not cover plot fees or gardener rules.
first_visit_tips: Email first, since meeting times and place are not on the website.
Ask about the next work day if you want to help out before getting a plot.

records.notes: The Upcoming Events page lists no dated events, and the site gives no year for its meetings. Instagram appears only as the handle @glenwoodcommunitygarden with no link, so no social link was recorded. The site says over 90 in-ground plots, while tier 1 (Neighborhood Garden Trust) gave 102; the summary keeps the tier 1 figure. PHS City Harvest is named as a program the garden takes part in, with no link on the page.

records.name: Global Philadelphia Association
records.summary: A nonprofit that brings together Philadelphia's international community. It runs a World Heritage City project, a global directory, a program for emerging international journalists, and a young professionals network.
records.what_you_do: Attend the public talks, artist panels, and town halls the group hosts, join its Young Professionals Network, or become a member. The group also lists unpaid internship and volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Public events are posted with their own dates on the upcoming events page. The Young Professionals group holds networking events in April, June and November, and its service days and tours are listed without set dates.

locations.label: Office
locations.address: Two Logan Square, 100 to 120 N 18th St, Suite 530

cost.text: Public event prices are not listed on the pages read. Membership levels run from $100 to $2,500, and the page does not say over what period.

first_step.how: Pick a public event from the upcoming events page and go, or sign up for the newsletter from the site footer to hear about the next one.
first_step.basis: Events are listed publicly with dates, and the newsletter sign up is clear. The event pages were not opened, so it is not confirmed whether each event is open to anyone.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public events include talks, artist panels, town halls and community celebrations. The listings do not say how long events last or what they cost, so check each event page before you go. Young Professionals take part in service days, guided tours and networking events at museums and historic venues.
first_visit_tips: Check each event page for cost and registration before you go.
The office is at Two Logan Square, 100 to 120 N 18th St, Suite 530.

records.notes: The membership page lists five levels: Community $100, Professional $250, Supporting $500, Sustaining $1,000 and Sponsoring $2,500. The page does not say the period these cover. Internships are unpaid with a $50 monthly travel stipend, 12 to 15 hours a week for at least 3 months, and interns must be in the Center City office at least one day a week. The site names the president as Zabeth Teelucksingh, while the contact name John F Smith III is kept from tier 1 and should be checked. The Young Professionals page does not say whether the network has a fee. The upcoming events page lists 12 events for October 2026 alone, and none of the event pages were opened.

records.name: Global Water Alliance
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that works on safe water, sanitation and hygiene around the world. It runs field projects and education programs, mentors young water professionals, and hosts talks and an annual conference.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on field projects, blog writing, events or fundraising, help plan the annual conference, or apply to the board. You can also become a member, attend talks, or donate.

schedule.text: Talks and events are posted with their own dates on the events page. The group holds a one-day annual conference in Philadelphia.

cost.text: Professional membership is $50 a year and student membership is $20 a year. Members get half off annual conference admission. Donations are optional.

first_step.how: Use the Get Involved form on the website to say whether you want to volunteer, write for the journal, join the conference, or help another way. Or become a member: $50 a year for professionals, $20 a year for students.
first_step.basis: Membership, volunteer and newsletter routes are listed publicly with a sign up form, and the group describes itself as mostly volunteer run. Talks are listed, but the page does not say which are open to the public.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most of the group is volunteers, so newcomers usually take part by helping with a project, writing for the blog, or helping run an event. The 18th annual conference was a one-day event on March 26, 2026, from 8:30 am to 4 pm, with breakfast and lunch provided and a reception afterward. The conference page does not state the ticket cost.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the next talk and whether it is open to the public.
Say which area you want to help with in the Get Involved form, so the group knows where to place you.

records.notes: The connect page says the conference is usually held in the fall, but the 18th annual conference page dates it to March 26, 2026, so the dated page is used. The events page lists the 2026 UN Water Conference (Dec 2 to 4, 2026) and the 11th World Water Forum (March 22 to 28, 2027, Riyadh), but neither page says whether it is open to the public, so neither is in the schedule. Corporate membership contact is GWAPhilly@gmail.com per the membership page. The IRS contact name is kept from tier 1.

records.name: Good Shepherd Community Church
records.summary: A church that does community outreach, with a stated focus on food needs and support for youth and seniors.
records.what_you_do: Attend worship and take part in the church's outreach and service work. The website does not list specific programs or service times.

locations.label: Address on IRS filing (not on the website)

first_step.how: Sign up with the email box on the homepage for news, then ask about service times, since the website does not list them.
first_step.basis: The site has no working contact link and no service times, so the way in is unclear. The only route found is the news sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The website does not say when services happen, how long they run or who usually attends. Outreach is described only in general terms, with food, youth and seniors named as priorities, so a first visit cannot be planned from the site alone.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the service times and address before you come, since the website does not list them.
The street address comes from the church's IRS filing, not from its website.

records.notes: The site's Contact Us link is an on-page anchor with no details. Its /contact, /about and /events paths returned HTTP 404. One web search for service times returned a different church with a similar name and no Philadelphia address, so it was not used. Status stays probably_active because the site is live but has no dated items. No service times, phone or email could be confirmed, so a person should check this record before it is trusted.

records.name: Grace of Miqlat Ministries
records.summary: A church that calls itself a place of refuge. It holds worship and Bible study, runs a children's Bible group, and welcomes visitors from the neighborhood.
records.what_you_do: Visit for worship, come to the Thursday adult Bible study, or join a Tuesday online class or a Saturday children's class. The church also offers notary and tax-filing help.

schedule.text: Adult Bible study on Thursdays, 6 to 7 pm. An online Tuesday Bible training class, 6 to 7 pm. The church home page lists Saturday children's classes at 3:30 to 4:30 pm. The children's Bible group is for ages 3 to 16 and meets weekly for about an hour.

locations.label: Tacony Library (listed for Saturday children's classes; confirm with the church)

cost.text: No fee is listed for classes. The site has donation buttons for a literacy fund.

first_step.how: Call 215-780-0633 or email gracemiqlat@live.com to confirm the times and where to meet, then come in for a visit.
first_step.basis: The church says visitors are welcome to come in for a visit and gives a phone number and email to arrange one.
first_step.what_to_expect: The website does not describe a first visit in detail. The church says its services are held at the main church, but it does not publish that street address, so ask for it when you call. The Thursday Bible study and the Tuesday online class each run one hour in the evening, and the children's group is for ages 3 to 16.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-780-0633 to confirm the time and place before you come.
Ask whether the Saturday children's class is on Zoom or in person at Tacony Library.
No fee is listed for classes, and donations are optional.

records.notes: The Saturday class time comes only from the home page, since the children's group page gives no day, time or place. The Wix social icons on the site point to Wix's accounts, not the church's, so no social links were recorded. The mailing address is a P.O. Box (17705, Philadelphia, PA 19135), not a meeting place, and was not recorded as a location. The site does not state a faith tradition, so audience.faith was left out. The services page also lists weddings, notary help and tax preparation through its Literacy Feeds the Masses program, with no days or prices given.

notes: Batch 050 covered seven groups, and all seven are publish. The six-fetch cap per group was reached for Girls Inc, Give Me My Roses, Global Philadelphia, Global Water Alliance and Grace of Miqlat. Glenwood and Good Shepherd used four fetches each. Girls Inc's Out of School Time, Summer Camps and School and Community Based pages were located but not read because of the cap. Good Shepherd's /contact, /about and /events paths returned HTTP 404, and its one web search returned a different church with a similar name, which was not used, so that record is thin and its confidence is low. No bot checks, 403s or rate limiting were seen. No form was submitted and the Girls Inc enrollment form was not opened. Contact names from IRS data were kept from tier 1, except Girls Inc's placeholder 'The Organization', which was dropped. Where the site names a different leader (Global Philadelphia), this is noted on the record.
